Please send in your questions and engage with us. ## Overview of New Features Now, let's dive into the new features of the 2025.2 version of Marvelous Designer. ### 3D Window Updates First, I want to introduce some updates in our 3D window. The foremost update allows users to convert a version into a component or configuration. To utilize this feature, we first need to import a virtual model. After downloading our virtual model, we can convert the version into a component or configuration, as it will match our virtual model. In the 3D window, you can directly select the custom configuration function. After selecting the custom configuration, you need to choose a configuration type. For instance, if we choose a hair type, we must enter a file, and the original hair will be automatically deleted. ### Importing 3D Files Now, we need to open a file, which should be in a general 3D file format, such as an OBJ file. After opening, you can see a preview of this file in the 3D window. You can then select its proportion, which refers to its original unit. When you change the proportion, the file will be automatically adjusted in the 3D window according to your settings. ### Shrink Charts and Saving Configurations You also have options to set a shrink chart. You can manually create some shrink charts or utilize the automatically created shrink chart. After completing the registration of this configuration, you will notice that this file is no longer an OBJ like before, but a new type of file that we have registered. For example, the hairstyle will be integrated with our virtual model. When adjusting the virtual model's skeleton, such as changing its movement, the hairstyle will move along with the head. Additionally, you can reactivate the virtual model to ensure that this hairstyle does not participate in calculations. This configuration is suitable for our virtual model, but if you switch to other virtual models, it cannot be used directly. ### Clothing Version Conversion In addition to the previous type, we can also convert a clothing version into a virtual model configuration. For instance, we can select the hat version and convert it into a configuration type of hat. After selecting the version, the desired version will be automatically selected in the object window. Once we finish converting, you will see that our conversion follows the display type in your 3D window. If you want to convert with thickness, make sure to enable the display thickness settings. If you do not enable the display thickness and proceed with the conversion, the converted version will lack thickness. ### Physical Type Configuration Our conversion configuration's physical type is a repeated physical type. When you choose the original physical setting as repeated, you can convert this version or component with physical properties. Similarly, for shoes, since they have a symmetrical structure, we only need to keep one side of the shoe file. After selecting all shoe parts, choose to automatically convert them to a custom configuration and select the configuration type as shoes. Make sure to select the direction of production to ensure it uses world coordinates for world symmetry. After symmetry, we can examine this converted shoe. ### Merging Components In addition to converting to virtual model configurations, we can also convert the version one by one into a copy. Previously, our glue tool worked point-to-point, but we can now merge many points on the fabric on one board, achieving some one-to-many converting effects. ### Adjusting Sewing Line Length Using the copy tool, we can adjust the length of the sewing line to control the distance between this component and the fabric. By adjusting the sewing line length, we can better manage the conflict between these components and the board. ## Software Model Simulation Now, let's discuss software model simulation. Our software model simulation can now be calculated through the GPU when it is turned on. For instance, the band added here exerts pressure on the hand. With GPU simulation support, the speed of calculation remains efficient. ### Zipper Optimization The new version also features zipper optimization. Additionally, when we select all and this zipper, the zipper belt will automatically synchronize the activation and deactivation effects. You can directly adjust the zipper in the 3D window, allowing you to pull it down from the collar. ### Zipper Attribute Editor In the zipper attribute editor, when we select the zipper head, we can see the settings for the zipper head, zipper, and zipper together. After adjusting the length of the zipper, there will be a contraction and release effect on both sides of the zipper. We also added a zipper setting in the upper right corner of the object window, allowing for unified management and adjustment of the unified type zipper. ### Fixed Pins and Everywhere Update Next, when we double-click a fixed pin on the board, all other fixed pins on the board will be selected simultaneously.
